name: Buenos Aires
tagline: Bife de chorizo with a Michelin star, a café haunted by Borges, and the La Boca joint where Francis Mallmann took Anthony Bourdain to eat.

Don Julio.description: The world's most acclaimed steakhouse: a Michelin star, a green star for sustainability, and #1 on Latin America's 50 Best. Critic Pietro Sorba (Clarín) gave it a perfect 5-star rating in 2021.

Café Tortoni.description: Buenos Aires' oldest café, since 1858. Borges, Gardel, and Cortázar all sat at its marble tables.

Don Carlos.description: A family-run joint in La Boca since 1970, with no menu — Carlitos himself decides what you eat. Francis Mallmann brought Anthony Bourdain here as the first stop of his Buenos Aires tour on "Parts Unknown" (2016).

Aramburu.description: A tasting menu of high technical precision from chef Gonzalo Aramburu, in Recoleta. Two Michelin stars.

Crizia.description: An oyster and seasonal fish specialist in Palermo. One Michelin star.

Trescha.description: A 16-course tasting menu for just 10 diners at the kitchen counter, inside a restored house in Villa Crespo. A Michelin star and No. 36 on Latin America's 50 Best 2025, led by chef Tomás Treschanski.

Gran Dabbang.description: A bold fusion of India and Southeast Asia made with Argentine products, in a tiny no-reservations Palermo storefront. No. 18 on Latin America's 50 Best 2024, led by chef Mariano Ramón.

Mishiguene.description: Ashkenazi, Sephardic and Israeli cuisine reinvented by chef Tomás Kalika in Palermo; the name means "crazy" in Yiddish. Featured on the Latin America's 50 Best list.

El Preferido de Palermo.description: A 1952 corner grocery store turned into an author-driven neighborhood joint by the Don Julio team. A Michelin Green Star and a spot on Latin America's 50 Best.

Niño Gordo.description: An "Asian grill" from the creators of La Carnicería in Palermo Soho: Argentine live-fire cooking with Asian spices and techniques. No. 34 on Latin America's 50 Best 2024.

Anchoíta.description: Enrique Piñeyro's Chacarita restaurant: aged meats, river fish and vegetables from its own garden, cooked over charcoal. A Michelin star and No. 73 on Latin America's 50 Best 2024.

Mengano.description: An "author-driven bodegón" in Palermo from chef Facundo Kelemen: porteño classics like revuelto gramajo or milanesa reworked with contemporary technique. A 2024 new entry on Latin America's 50 Best.

Elena.description: The Four Seasons' flagship restaurant in Recoleta, with an open dry-aging chamber for meats. Recognized by the Michelin Guide Argentina and featured for several years on Latin America's 50 Best.

La Carnicería.description: A small, informal grill from chefs Germán Sitz and Pedro Peña in Palermo Soho, sister restaurant to Niño Gordo, focused on signature cuts. Listed on 50 Best Discovery.

Corte Comedor.description: A modern steakhouse in Belgrano, next to its own butcher shop, with a focus on meat traceability and dry-aging. Included in the Michelin Guide Argentina.

Roux.description: A fine-dining restaurant by Martín Rebaudino specializing in fish, shellfish and seasonal produce, with an extensive wine list.

BASA.description: A multi-level restaurant and bar near Plaza San Martín, serving Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. Included in the 2024 Michelin Guide.

Osaka.description: Nikkei (Japanese-Peruvian) cuisine in Puerto Madero, one of the city's reference points for the genre since the early 2000s.

Sudestada.description: Uncompromising Thai and Vietnamese cooking in Palermo Hollywood, with pad thai and curries that made it a pioneer of the genre in the city.

La Mar Cebichería.description: Peruvian chef Gastón Acurio's cebichería in Palermo, serving ceviches, tiraditos and cocktails on an open-air patio.

Todos Contentos.description: A family-run canteen in Belgrano's Chinatown, a decades-long reference point for dim sum in Buenos Aires.

Sarkis.description: A temple of Armenian cooking in Villa Crespo since 1982, founded by the Katabian family: nightly lines for the hummus, eggplant and kibbeh.

Piegari.description: A porteño landmark of Italian cooking in Puerto Madero since the 1990s, known for its house-made pastas and gala-style setting.

Oviedo.description: Since 1986, a porteño reference for seafood with Galician roots and a cellar of more than 18,000 bottles, founded by Emilio Garip.

La Brigada.description: A San Telmo steakhouse since 1992, where the waiter cuts the bife de chorizo with a spoon to show how well it's cooked. One of the historic grills tied to Anthony Bourdain's Argentina travels.

Cabaña Las Lilas.description: An emblematic Puerto Madero steakhouse opened in 1995, born from the family's own cattle ranch, with a wine list recognized by Wine Spectator.

La Cabrera.description: One of Palermo Soho's most popular steakhouses, known for its free side dishes and the "meat happy hour" after-work ritual devised by chef Gastón Riveira.

El Pobre Luis.description: A "River Plate" steakhouse in Belgrano's Chinatown, founded in 1986 by Uruguayan Luis Acuña; its walls are covered in football pennants.

El Obrero.description: A La Boca bodegón founded in 1954 by Marcelino Castro to feed dockworkers and meatpacking-plant employees; declared a Site of Cultural Interest in 2018.

Sabot.description: A classic business-lunch spot in the microcentro since 1969, with a small menu and old-school service.

Pippo.description: A porteño bodegón with nearly 90 years of history: abundant portions, accessible prices, and the atmosphere of old Buenos Aires.

Los Galgos.description: A Notable Bar in San Nicolás turned into a fashionable bodegón without losing its old-world bar and facade; famous for revuelto gramajo and milanesa.

Club Eros.description: A bodegón operating inside a Palermo neighborhood social club, serving gnocchi and bife de chorizo among members who play football and truco.

El Sanjuanino.description: A Recoleta institution with over half a century of history, known for empanadas fried to order and its locro stew.

La Cocina.description: A small Recoleta spot run by a family from Catamarca for 40 years, specializing in oven-baked Northern-style empanadas.

Güerrín.description: A temple of porteño pizza on Av. Corrientes since 1932: generous mozzarella eaten standing at the counter, as tradition dictates.

Banchero.description: A pizzeria with over 90 years of history on Av. Corrientes, birthplace of the fugazza con queso.

El Cuartito.description: A Retiro pizzeria since 1934, its walls covered in sports memorabilia, with its famous fugazzeta as the star.

Angelín.description: A Villa Crespo pizzeria since 1938, creator of the cheeseless, oversized "pizza cancha."

Siamo nel Forno.description: A reference point for true Neapolitan pizza in Palermo Hollywood, with a wood-fired oven and long-fermented dough.

Kentucky.description: A Palermo pizzeria since 1942, known for its thick crust and its round-the-clock weekend hours.

Florería Atlántico.description: A speakeasy hidden behind a fridge door in a Recoleta flower shop, created by bartender Tato Giovannoni. It reached No. 3 on The World's 50 Best Bars in 2019.

Presidente Bar.description: An elegant Recoleta cocktail bar created by bartender Seba García, with a winter garden and a menu mixing classics with house creations. It climbed to No. 33 on The World's 50 Best Bars.

Milión.description: A restaurant and bar inside a 1913 French-style mansion in Recoleta, with a secret garden and period salons; open since 1999.

Buller Brewing Company.description: A pioneer of craft beer in Buenos Aires since 1999, with a brewpub and rooftop terrace in Recoleta.

Grand Bar Danzón.description: A Palermo wine bar with roughly 300 Argentine labels, a porteño reference point for wine by the glass.

Cadore.description: An Italian ice cream shop founded in 1957 on Av. Corrientes by the Olivotti family; declared a Site of Cultural Interest and named among the world's best by National Geographic.

Rapa Nui.description: A Patagonian ice cream and chocolate chain born in Bariloche in 1996, with a flagship shop facing Plaza San Martín.

Café La Biela.description: Buenos Aires' oldest still-operating bar, dating to 1850, across from the Recoleta cemetery; a historic meeting point for Formula 1 and motor-racing drivers.

Las Violetas.description: An Almagro confitería opened in 1884, with original stained glass and pastries that earned it the "Best Notable Café" title in 2017.

El Gato Negro.description: A café, spice shop and gourmet store on Av. Corrientes since 1928, known for its classic tea and cinnamon aroma.

La Giralda.description: A porteño temple of hot chocolate and churros since 1930, in the heart of the Av. Corrientes theater district.

Café de los Angelitos.description: An 1890 café where Carlos Gardel launched his career alongside José Razzano; today it also operates as a tango venue.

Bar Iberia.description: A Spanish-flavored Notable Bar in Montserrat, one of the venues protected as porteño cultural heritage.

Bar El Federal.description: A former pulpería and general store in San Telmo, now a Notable Bar with its original wooden counter and shelving.

El Desnivel.description: A San Telmo bodegón since 1993, popular with tourists for its abundant, fairly priced grilled meats.

Café La Poesía.description: A Notable Bar in San Telmo that in the 1960s was a meeting point for poets, founded by poet Rubén Derlis himself.

Confitería Ideal.description: A porteño confitería from 1912, famous for its tea room and its historic upstairs milonga; it reopened in 2022 after a full restoration.

Chiquilín.description: A restaurant from 1927 in San Nicolás that inspired the Piazzolla-Ferrer tango "Chiquilín de Bachín"; bodegón cooking with a grill-house edge.

Bar Plaza Dorrego.description: A Notable Bar facing San Telmo's Plaza Dorrego, at the heart of the Sunday antiques fair.

Los 36 Billares.description: A historic billiards hall and café on Av. de Mayo, a stage for tango and porteño bohemia since the early 20th century.

London City.description: A notable café on Av. de Mayo where, according to porteño literary lore, Julio Cortázar wrote part of "Los premios."

Confitería Richmond.description: A confitería on Calle Florida, a classic salon for chess games and porteño conversation for decades.

El Querandí.description: A Notable Bar in Montserrat that also operates as a tango venue, in an early-20th-century building.

Esquina Homero Manzi.description: A historic Boedo corner named for tango poet Homero Manzi, today a tango hall and restaurant.

Bar Británico.description: A Notable Bar in San Telmo, open 24 hours across from Parque Lezama; it appears in Ernesto Sabato's novel "On Heroes and Tombs."

Bar Sur.description: A San Telmo tango bar with over a century of history, popular with visitors for its intimate live tango shows.

Bar Seddon.description: A classic English-style Notable Bar in Montserrat, operating on the same corner for over a century.

Plaza Bar.description: A classic bar inside Retiro's historic Marriott Plaza Hotel, serving drinks and hospitality for over a century.

Florida Garden.description: A Retiro café on Calle Florida, a traditional meeting point for porteño writers like Bioy Casares.

La Academia.description: A Notable Café in Balvanera on Av. Callao, one of the traditional venues protected by the city's Notable Bars program.

Café Margot.description: A Notable Bar in Boedo since 1904, famous for its pickled-turkey sandwich and the legend of a visit from Juan Domingo Perón.

El Progreso.description: A bar and billiards hall in Barracas, one of the city's oldest, tied to the culture of porteño billiards.

Los Laureles.description: A bodegón and Notable Bar in Barracas with over a century of history, a classic of porteño neighborhood cooking.

La Perla.description: A Notable Bar on La Boca's waterfront, facing the Riachuelo, painted and photographed for decades by neighborhood artists.

Café Tabac.description: A Notable Bar on Av. del Libertador in Palermo, one of the venues protected as porteño cultural heritage.

Bar Los Andes.description: A Notable Bar in Palermo on Avenida Scalabrini Ortiz, with a facade and counter from another era.

Varela Varelita.description: A Notable Bar in Palermo on Scalabrini Ortiz, a traditional neighborhood corner turned cultural heritage site.

Petit Colón.description: A Notable Café in San Nicolás steps from Teatro Colón, historically frequented by musicians and opera singers.

The Brighton.description: An English-style Notable Bar in San Nicolás, with wood paneling and the feel of a British club.

Bar de Cao.description: A Notable Bar in San Cristóbal on Avenida Independencia, one of the corner-store bars recognized by the city.

Miramar.description: A Notable Bar in San Cristóbal, a classic porteño corner store turned neighborhood café and restaurant.

El Banderín.description: A Notable Bar in Almagro decorated with thousands of football-club pennants collected over the decades.

El Símbolo.description: A Notable Café in Almagro on Av. Corrientes, one of the traditional venues in the neighborhood of tango.

Café Roma.description: A Notable Café in La Boca, on Calle Olavarría, a witness to neighborhood life alongside the Riachuelo.

Café El Estaño 1880.description: A Notable Café in La Boca near Caminito, decorated like a late-19th-century general store.

Chan Chan.description: One of Buenos Aires' oldest and most popular Peruvian restaurants, in the heart of downtown, known for its lomo saltado and ají de gallina.

Isabel.description: A Palermo Soho restaurant and bar serving Nikkei food and cocktails, a modern classic of Palermo nightlife.

Duhau Restaurante & Vinoteca.description: The restaurant of the Palacio Duhau - Park Hyatt in Recoleta, with an author-driven menu and one of the city's most complete wine cellars; recommended by the Michelin Guide.

Le Grill.description: An upscale steakhouse inside the Faena Hotel in Puerto Madero, serving premium cuts in a highly produced setting.

Mercado de San Telmo.description: An iron-and-glass market opened in 1897, today mixing antiques stalls with food ranging from choripán to dumplings.

La Puerto Rico.description: A Montserrat café and coffee roastery operating since 1887, one of the oldest in Buenos Aires.

Bar Bidou.description: A Notable Bar in San Nicolás on Av. Roque Sáenz Peña, one of the traditional venues protected by the city.

El Coleccionista.description: A Notable Café in Caballito on Av. Rivadavia, a traditional neighborhood meeting point.

Victoria.description: A Notable Bar in Montserrat on Av. Entre Ríos, one of the historic corner-store bars recognized by the city.

Café Don Juan.description: A Notable Café in the Villa Santa Rita neighborhood, one of the traditional local venues protected as porteño cultural heritage.

El Viejo Buzón.description: A Notable Bar in Caballito on Calle Neuquén, a classic neighborhood corner store turned bar with history.

Ocho Esquinas.description: A Notable Bar in Chacarita on Av. Forest, a traditional neighborhood meeting point recognized by the city.

Paulín.description: A Notable Café in San Nicolás on Calle Sarmiento, one of the historic venues of the porteño microcentro.

Café Montserrat.description: A Notable Café in the Montserrat neighborhood on Calle San José, a traditional porteño corner turned cultural heritage site.
